**SECTION D: ESSAY**

*Write an essay of about 200 - 250 words on any ONE of the following topics.*

questions.enonce_markdown: **1.** « Mothers are more important in the family than fathers. » Discuss this statement with your classmate. (Essay, 200-250 words)
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un sujet du type « Discuss this statement » exige une introduction qui reformule le sujet et annonce le plan, un développement qui examine posément le pour et le contre (ou nuance l'affirmation) avec des arguments illustrés d'exemples concrets, et une conclusion qui prend position de façon raisonnée sans se contenter de répéter l'introduction.

**Plan retenu (essai argumentatif nuancé) :**

- **Introduction** : reformulation du sujet + annonce que la réponse dépend du type d'importance considéré.
- **Développement, partie 1** : arguments en faveur du rôle central de la mère (grossesse, petite enfance, gestion du foyer).
- **Développement, partie 2** : arguments en faveur du rôle irremplaçable du père (discipline, modèle, protection).
- **Synthèse** : les deux rôles sont complémentaires plutôt que hiérarchisables.
- **Conclusion** : prise de position raisonnée qui refuse le classement simple proposé par le sujet, sans se contenter de répéter l'introduction.

**Rédaction modèle complète (environ 230 mots) :**

Families are the foundation of every society, and within them, both parents are expected to play a crucial role in raising children. However, the statement that mothers are more important than fathers in the family deserves careful discussion, because everything depends on what kind of importance is being considered.

On one hand, mothers are often the ones who carry the pregnancy, breastfeed the baby, and spend the most time with young children during their early, most formative years. In many African households, it is the mother who manages daily domestic life, cooks, monitors school work, and provides emotional comfort. This closeness creates a special bond that can make a mother's presence feel irreplaceable.

On the other hand, fathers also play an essential role that cannot be reduced to financial provision alone. A father teaches discipline, models responsible behaviour for his sons, and often represents authority and protection within the household. Children who grow up without a present father figure frequently struggle with a sense of security and guidance that a mother, however devoted, cannot always provide alone.

In reality, neither parent's role can be measured as simply "more important" than the other, because a family functions best when both parents complement each other. A mother's nurturing and a father's guidance work together, not in competition, to build a balanced and secure environment for children to grow up in.

In conclusion, rather than ranking mothers above fathers, it is more accurate to recognise that both parents bring irreplaceable and complementary contributions to family life. A family thrives not because one parent matters more, but because both play their part fully.

questions.enonce_markdown: **2.** You are a health worker sent to your village where early marriages are still a problem. Make a speech sensitizing the rural population on the dangers of this practice. (Essay, 200-250 words)
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un discours de sensibilisation s'ouvre par une formule d'adresse au public et une accroche qui capte l'attention, développe ensuite les dangers concrets du problème visé avec des exemples parlants, et se termine par un appel à l'action direct, adressé au public présent.

**Plan retenu (speech) :**

- **Adresse d'ouverture + accroche** : salutation au public, phrase qui capte l'attention sur l'enjeu.
- **Danger 1** : risques pour la santé de la mère adolescente (grossesses à risque, complications à l'accouchement).
- **Danger 2** : interruption de la scolarité et réduction des perspectives économiques futures.
- **Danger 3** : déséquilibre de pouvoir dans le couple, risque de violence domestique.
- **Appel à l'action + clôture** : demande concrète au public, remerciement.

**Extrait rédigé (à développer jusqu'à 200-250 mots le jour de l'examen) :**

"Good morning, dear parents and elders of our village. I stand before you today to talk about a problem that is silently destroying the future of our daughters: early marriage.

First, early marriage puts a young girl's health in serious danger. Her body is often not yet ready for pregnancy, and this can lead to difficult deliveries and, in the worst cases, death. Second, when a girl is married off early, she is forced to leave school, which closes the door to better job opportunities for the rest of her life. Third, a very young wife often has no voice in her own home, which can expose her to violence and mistreatment.

I therefore urge every parent here today to let your daughters finish their education before thinking of marriage, and to remember that the law of our country protects children from being married too young. Thank you for listening."

Il ne reste plus, le jour de l'examen, qu'à développer chaque danger sur 2-3 phrases supplémentaires pour atteindre les 200-250 mots demandés, en gardant la même structure.

rappels_de_methode.contenu_markdown: Un discours de sensibilisation s'ouvre par une formule d'adresse au public et une accroche qui capte l'attention, développe ensuite les dangers concrets du problème visé avec des exemples parlants, et se termine par un appel à l'action direct, adressé au public présent.

questions.enonce_markdown: **3.** Write a report to the chief of your village on some negative happenings in your area. Why are they negative? What do you think should be done to ameliorate the situation? (Essay, 200-250 words)
questions.corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode
Un rapport formel adressé à une autorité (ici le chef de village) s'ouvre par un en-tête précisant l'expéditeur, le destinataire, la date et l'objet, développe les faits observés de façon factuelle et organisée, puis propose des recommandations concrètes avant une formule de clôture respectueuse.

**Plan retenu (report) :**

- **En-tête** : To (destinataire), From (expéditeur), Date, Subject (objet du rapport).
- **Introduction** : rappel bref du contexte et de l'objectif du rapport.
- **Corps du rapport (faits observés)** : 2 à 3 problèmes concrets, chacun avec pourquoi il est négatif.
- **Recommandations** : une mesure concrète par problème soulevé.
- **Formule de clôture respectueuse**.

**Plan détaillé rédigé (à développer jusqu'à 200-250 mots le jour de l'examen) :**

To: The Chief of ……… Village
From: ……… (name of the reporter)
Date: ………
Subject: Report on negative happenings in the village

"I am writing this report to bring to your attention some negative happenings observed in our village over the past months, so that appropriate action can be taken.

First, many young people have taken to littering the main market and the stream with plastic waste. This is negative because it pollutes our only source of drinking water and can cause diseases such as cholera. Second, unemployed youths have started gathering at the village square late at night, which has led to an increase in theft cases. This creates fear and insecurity among villagers, especially women and the elderly. Third, some farmers have been cutting down trees along the riverbank without replanting, which is gradually causing soil erosion.

I therefore recommend that a village clean-up committee be created to organise regular cleaning of the market and the stream, that a youth employment programme be considered to keep idle young people busy, and that a rule be introduced requiring anyone who cuts a tree to plant two in its place.

I hope Your Majesty will consider these observations and recommendations for the well-being of the whole village."

Il suffit, le jour de l'examen, de développer chaque paragraphe sur 1-2 phrases supplémentaires pour atteindre les 200-250 mots demandés, en conservant cette structure en quatre temps.
